Read Bank of Japan observations for a hierarchy layer

Source: R/api.R
read_boj_layer.Rd

Fetches the observations selected by the official BOJ Time-Series Data Search getDataLayer route. A layer is one to five hierarchy values, with * selecting all values at a level. Every NEXTPOSITION cursor is followed and the returned observations use the same schema as read_boj_series(). Use read_boj_series() when the desired series codes are already known.

Usage

read_boj_layer(
  db,
  frequency,
  layer,
  start_date = NULL,
  end_date = NULL,
  language = "en",
  format = "json",
  cache_dir = boj_cache_dir(),
  refresh = FALSE,
  offline = FALSE,
  max_age = 24 * 60 * 60,
  timeout = 30,
  retries = 3L,
  wait = 1,
  max_bytes = 128 * 1024^2,
  max_pages = 100L,
  max_cells = 1000000L,
  max_series = 1250L,
  deadline = NULL
)

Arguments

db

A BOJ database identifier, such as "FM08"; it is normalized to uppercase and may still be rejected by the API if unknown.

frequency

Observation frequency code: "CY", "FY", "CH", "FH", "Q", "M", "W", or "D". Matching is case-insensitive.

layer

One to five comma-separated non-negative integer hierarchy values, or * as a wildcard at a level. A numeric vector is collapsed with commas; an empty value, more than five values, or any other character raises readboj_parameter_error.

start_date

Optional inclusive YYYY or YYYYPP period bound; NULL omits it from the request.

end_date

Optional inclusive YYYY or YYYYPP period bound; NULL omits it. If both bounds are supplied, start_date must not be later.

language

Response language, exactly "en" or "jp".

format

Response format, "json" or "csv"; matching is case-insensitive.

cache_dir

Character path to the content-addressed response cache; see read_boj_series() and boj_cache_dir().

refresh

Logical flag to bypass a current request snapshot.

offline

Logical flag requiring a valid cached snapshot and disabling network access.

max_age

Non-negative cache age in seconds, or Inf; the default is 24 hours.

timeout

Non-negative per-attempt HTTP timeout in seconds; the default is 30 seconds.

retries

Non-negative whole-number transient-failure retry count; the default is 3.

wait

Non-negative seconds between pages and retries; skipped offline.

max_bytes

Positive decompressed response-byte bound per page; the default is 128 MiB.

max_pages

Positive whole-number page bound for this layer request; the default is 100.

max_cells

Positive whole-number observation-row bound across all pages; the default is 1,000,000.

max_series

Positive whole-number maximum distinct series allowed in the result; the default is 1,250.

deadline

Optional absolute one-element POSIXct/POSIXlt deadline shared by all requests, retries and delays. A bounded default is created when omitted.

Value

An ungrouped base data.frame with row names reset and the same exact observation columns and types as read_boj_series(): character db, series_code, name_en, name_jp, unit_en, unit_jp, frequency, category_en, category_jp, and period; Date last_update and date; numeric value; and character raw_value and value_status, in that column order. A readboj_provenance attribute records the layer query, page identities, hashes, cache status, parser schema and package version. No duplicate observation identity is collapsed.

Details

frequency is normalized to uppercase and must be one of CY, FY, CH, FH, Q, M, W, or D; layer values are non-negative integers or *. A numeric layer vector is joined with commas before validation. The request is bounded by max_pages and max_cells, then fails with readboj_size_error if more than max_series distinct series are returned; it is not silently truncated. Network, HTTPS-host, cache, offline and deadline behavior is the same as read_boj_series().

Errors and side effects

Invalid parameters, malformed or changed BOJ responses, pagination loops, duplicate identities, result bounds, transport failures and unavailable offline snapshots raise typed readboj_*_error conditions. The function may access the network and write only successful response snapshots below cache_dir; it does not intentionally issue warnings.

Examples

if (identical(Sys.getenv("READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES"), "true")) {
  read_boj_layer(
    db = "IR01", frequency = "D", layer = "*",
    start_date = "202607", end_date = "202607", format = "csv",
    cache_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "readboj-live-example-cache"),
    timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 8 * 1024^2,
    max_pages = 2L, max_cells = 1000L, max_series = 100L
  )
} else {
  message("Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run the live BOJ example.")
}
#> Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run the live BOJ example.
